title: Butter Chicken
summary: Yoghurt-marinated chicken thighs are charred under the grill, then finished in a buttery tomato, cream and garam masala sauce.
equipment: foil-lined baking tray with a rack
large deep frying pan or sauté pan (28 cm)

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: about 1 tsp; optional, only if the tomatoes are sharp

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, garam masala, chilli powder and salt, then cover and refrigerate for 1-12 hours. The yoghurt's mild acidity tenderises the meat while the spices start to flavour it right through.

steps.title: Char under the grill
steps.text: Spread the marinated chicken on the rack and grill (broiler) on high for 8-10 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. It doesn't need to be fully cooked yet, since it will finish gently in the sauce.

steps.title: Build the sauce base
steps.text: Melt the butter with the oil in the pan over medium heat, then cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 8-10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the ground spices, apart from the sauce's garam masala, for 30 seconds until fragrant - this brief blooming in hot fat is what wakes up their flavour.

steps.title: Simmer the tomato base
steps.text: Stir in the tomato purée for 1 minute, then add the tinned tomatoes, water and salt. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until thickened, then blend the sauce smooth, taking care as it will be hot.

steps.title: Finish and cook the chicken through
steps.text: Return the sauce to the pan and add the chicken and any juices and simmer gently for 4-5 minutes, then stir in the cream, fenugreek leaves and the sauce's garam masala and simmer for 4-5 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 74°C and the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Taste and serve
steps.text: Taste the sauce and add the sugar only if the tomatoes taste sharp. Scatter with coriander and serve with rice or naan.

tips: Char the chicken under a hot grill rather than cooking it through at this stage - it finishes cooking in the sauce, which keeps it juicy.
Common mistake: blending the sauce while it's still thin and raw-tasting. Simmering it down first concentrates the flavour before you purée it.
Cook the onion slowly until truly soft and golden, a full 8-10 minutes; its sweetness rounds out the tomato and cream.
Only add sugar if the tomatoes are noticeably sharp - good tinned tomatoes rarely need it.
Crush the dried fenugreek leaves between your fingers before adding; it releases their distinctive aroma.
safety: Hot sauce can spit and splatter in the blender; blend it carefully, in batches if needed.
storage: Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat gently, stirring often, until piping hot throughout (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
